events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.50 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip ran 11.6 km against an 8.4 km optimal route [F1], and code has already settled deviation over tolerance: billed − optimal = 3.19 km [F4][RD-1]. The only off-route segment is F3, 12:11–12:17, 4.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.58 km, adding 2.88 km [F3]. So the case turns on whether that segment is exempt under RD-3/RD-5.

Notice and agreement (RD-5): the driver asked at 12:07 whether to take another way because of traffic on the Ayer Rajah Expressway [F7]; the rider answered at 12:08, "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4" [F8]. That is a RIDER message sent before the segment began at 12:11, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9]. The words are a general route choice ("can") with one road ruled out — so excluded_road = Clementi Avenue 4, not named_road [F8][RD-5].

Scope: the trace lists the roads actually driven, and CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 is among them [F3]. The rider's words expressly rule that road out, so the agreement to "another way" does not cover this segment: the segment drove the one road the rider excluded, which is exactly the "counts" consequence of RD-5 for a ruled-out road. Ground: general_route_consent with excluded_road = Clementi Avenue 4, driven → counts; finding = counts.

The driver's statement that "the rider said can, so I went round" [F10] is written after the trip and is not part of the chat, so it cannot expand the scope of the 12:08 agreement [RD-5]. The traffic record (AYER RAJAYAH Expressway band 2, congestion, during 11:58–12:17 [F11]) gives the segment a traffic reason under RD-4, which is why the trace shows no driver violation; but RD-4 never exempts a segment — under RD-2 the amount turns only on whether the rider agreed to the route [RD-2][RD-5].

RD-3 is not engaged: the rider named no place she wanted to go, and no stop is measured in this segment; she only excluded a road, which is RD-5 territory, not RD-3 [F8][RD-3].

Amount: refundable km = deviation − exempt km = 3.19 km − 0 km exempt = 3.19 km; 3.19 km × $1.4096/km = $4.4966 → $4.50 [F4][RD-2]. That is the excess distance fare already billed at $4.50 on record [F4]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge is 1.0× here [F5][RD-2].

RD-6: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17], so no flag_account. The earlier route disputes on both profiles are profile facts and never decide this case [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages, and the driver's statement [F7][F8][F10] — a route argument only; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern: none.

Evidence: the record settles everything the ruling needs — measured GPS distances [F1][F3], the fare breakdown and per-km rate [F4], a complete timestamped chat with the rider's message before the segment [F8][F9], and traffic data [F11]. evidence_status: sufficient.

We can see there was heavy traffic at the time, which is why no violation is recorded. Nothing further is needed from you.
